requirements.text: Must be actively enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program at the time of application and returning to complete the degree after the co-op.
Available to start full-time between December 2027 and August 2028.
Available to work full-time (40 hours/week) at an IBM location for 16 weeks between Jan 19 - May 7.
Co-op requires a full-time commitment; students should not be enrolled in concurrent coursework during the co-op term.
Strong software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, software design, and testing.
Proficiency in Python and experience building applications or services that integrate APIs.

Hands-on experience building an application or working prototype with LLMs. You can explain what you built, how you integrated the model, and how you tested its behavior. Experience may come from personal, academic, open-source, or internship projects.
A systematic debugging mindset: you can investigate failures, test assumptions, and reason about how application code, data, models, and underlying systems interact.
Ability to translate a problem into clear requirements, prompts, and testable acceptance criteria, and critically evaluate AI-generated code and responses.
Familiarity with Git, clear technical communication, and the ability to learn quickly and collaborate on a team.
AI agents and tool or function calling; retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), embeddings, vector databases, or Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Independent AI projects, open-source contributions, or experiments beyond assigned coursework that demonstrate initiative and thoughtful engineering decisions.
Additional programming experience in JavaScript/TypeScript or Go, and familiarity with distributed systems or microservices.
Operating system concepts such as concurrency, multithreading, and memory management; relational databases and SQL.
Cloud and container technologies such as Docker, Kubernetes, or OpenShift; observability, search, or real-time data processing tools such as OpenSearch or Kafka.
AI evaluation, anomaly detection, or experience measuring and improving model accuracy, latency, and reliability.
